chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Salim ibn al-Baraa al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Bareed al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawab al-Hubbari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, who said: My brother Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father, from his forefathers, may Allah's blessings be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said:

Four things — whoever possesses them, Allah shall inscribe him among the people of Paradise: One whose safeguard is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that I, Muhammad, am the Messenger of Allah; and one who, when Allah bestows a blessing upon him, says: 'Praise be to Allah'; and one who, when he commits a sin, says: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah'; and one who, when afflicted by a calamity, says: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return.'

key_terms.شَهَادَة: testimony of faith (shahada) — the declaration of God's oneness and Muhammad's prophethood
key_terms.عِصْمَة: safeguard/protection — referring to the shahada as a spiritual anchor

ai.seo_question: What are the four virtues that guarantee a person's place in Paradise according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) teaches that four spiritual practices guarantee a person's place in Paradise: holding firm to the declaration of faith (shahada), expressing gratitude (al-hamdulillah) upon receiving blessings, seeking forgiveness (istighfar) after sinning, and reciting the Quranic phrase of returning to God (inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un) upon facing calamity. This hadith, transmitted through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizes that a believer's response in every life circumstance — abundance, sin, or affliction — should be oriented toward God.
